generations.rawResponse: {"disposition":"assist","answer":"I’d switch to 0-1 BFS, replacing the FIFO queue with a deque: improved zero-weight neighbors go to the front, and improved one-weight neighbors go to the back. Initialize the source distance to zero and all others to infinity; only when dist[u] + weight is smaller than dist[v] do I update v’s distance and parent and enqueue it. The old visited-on-enqueue rule no longer holds, because a discovered vertex may later get a shorter path; strict improvement also prevents zero-weight cycles from causing endless updates. With the same adjacency list, time remains O(V + E)—here, 10,000 vertices and 50,000 edges—and auxiliary space remains O(V)."}
generations.answer: I’d switch to 0-1 BFS, replacing the FIFO queue with a deque: improved zero-weight neighbors go to the front, and improved one-weight neighbors go to the back. Initialize the source distance to zero and all others to infinity; only when dist[u] + weight is smaller than dist[v] do I update v’s distance and parent and enqueue it. The old visited-on-enqueue rule no longer holds, because a discovered vertex may later get a shorter path; strict improvement also prevents zero-weight cycles from causing endless updates. With the same adjacency list, time remains O(V + E)—here, 10,000 vertices and 50,000 edges—and auxiliary space remains O(V).
